title: Unary less-than machine
statement: Consider a two-register machine with one available decider and the eight labels start, test, compare, three intermediate labels, yes, and no. At start it validates the input as a unary-prefixed canonical binary word, rejecting invalid inputs; at test it calls the available decider on the unary prefix with register 1 as its argument, branching to no if the call accepts and to compare otherwise. At compare it accepts if the input's binary payload equals register 1; otherwise it increments register 1, then increments register 2 twice, and returns to test. The yes label accepts and the no label rejects.
caveat: The prose describes the transition table and its instruction meanings; the behavior of the called decider is not otherwise specified.
